questions.knowledge_point: Determining the Image of an Object Formed by a Singular Transformation
questions.problem:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14072249/assets/fee79ec0b214a4ba87400b4b8c9dab2c623878d067821c572b26ae241625c48a.png)

Consider the linear transformation $T$ with matrix representation $T,$ given by

$$
T=[\begin{aligned}2 & 1 \\ 10 & 5\end{aligned}].
$$

Which of the following is the image of the triangle shown above under the action of $T?$
questions.worked_solution:
To find the image of the triangle under the action of $T$, we first create a matrix $X$ containing all of the vertices of the triangle:

$$
X=[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 2 \\ 0 & 1 & 1\end{aligned}].
$$

Now, we compute the image of $X$ under the action of $T$ by calculating the matrix product $TX:$

$$
\begin{aligned}TX & =[\begin{aligned}2 & 1 \\ 10 & 5\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 2 \\ 0 & 1 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}2 & 3 & 5 \\ 10 & 15 & 25\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the coordinates of the image's vertices are $(2,10)$, $(3,15)$, and  $(5,25).$  Notice that all three points lie on the same line.

questions.worked_solution:
To find the image of the triangle under the action of $T$, we first create a matrix $X$ containing all of the vertices of the triangle:

$$
X=[\begin{aligned}0 & 2 & 1 \\ 1 & 0 & 2\end{aligned}].
$$

Now, we compute the image of $X$ under the action of $T$ by calculating the matrix product $TX:$

$$
\begin{aligned}TX & =[\begin{aligned}0 & 3 \\ 0 & -6\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}0 & 2 & 1 \\ 1 & 0 & 2\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}3 & 0 & 6 \\ -6 & 0 & -12\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the coordinates of the image's vertices are $(3,-6)$, $(0,0),$ $(6,-12).$ Notice that all three points lie on the same line.

questions.knowledge_point: Calculating the Coordinates of an Image Formed by a Singular Transformation
questions.problem:
Consider the linear transformation $T$ with matrix representation $T,$ given by

$$
T=[\begin{aligned}-2 & 3 \\ 6 & -9\end{aligned}].
$$

A triangle $S$ has vertices at $(-1,3),(0,-2),$ and $(4,1).$ Which of the following are coordinates of the vertices of ${S}^{′},$ the image of $S$ under the action of $T?$

- $(-11,3)$
- $(-5,15)$
- $(18,-3)$
questions.worked_solution:
To find the image of $S$ under the action of $T$, we first create a matrix $X$ containing all of the vertices of $S:$

$$
X=[\begin{aligned}-1 & 0 & 4 \\ 3 & -2 & 1\end{aligned}].
$$

Now, we compute the image of $X$ under $T$ by calculating the matrix product $TX:$

$$
\begin{aligned}TX & =[\begin{aligned}-2 & 3 \\ 6 & -9\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}-1 & 0 & 4 \\ 3 & -2 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}11 & -6 & -5 \\ -33 & 18 & 15\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the coordinates of the respective vertices of ${S}^{′}$ are $(11,-33)$, $(-6,18)$ and $(-5,15).$ 

So, the correct answer is "II only."

questions.knowledge_point: Identifying the Type of Image Formed by a Linear Transformation
questions.problem:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14072249/assets/da6c0fb32e62b6effe133c527fee528c47b6f1c8dc7dd1d77d7d04f42b4c3d2b.png)

Consider the linear transformation $T$ with matrix representation $T,$ given by

$$
T=[\begin{aligned}0 & 0 \\ 0 & 0\end{aligned}].
$$

What would be the image of the quadrilateral shown above under the action of $T?$
questions.worked_solution:
Recall that for any linear transformation $T$ with associated $2\times 2$ matrix $T,$ we have one of the following three possibilities:

- If $T$ is non-singular, i.e., $det(T)\ne 0,$ then the image of a two-dimensional object is a two-dimensional object. In particular, the image of a polygon with $n$ vertices is a polygon with $n$ vertices.

- If $T$ is singular, i.e., $det(T)=0,$ we have two additional subcases:

- If $T$ has at least one nonzero entry, then the image of a two-dimensional object is a one-dimensional line segment.

- If $T$ is the zero matrix, then the image of a two-dimensional object is the point $(0,0),$ the origin of the coordinate system.

Since $T$ is the zero matrix, the image of our object under the action of $T$ is the origin.

choices.value: A point, different from the origin
The origin $O$ of the coordinate system

answer_fields.correct_value: The origin $O$ of the coordinate system

questions.knowledge_point: Identifying the Type of Image Formed by a Linear Transformation
questions.problem:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14072249/assets/e6d0ce147aec90c3840a893e36596fbadf981ff96559f65d055f4486406cca7f.png)

Consider the linear transformation $T$ with matrix representation $T,$ given by

$$
T=[\begin{aligned}-1 & 1 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}].
$$

What would be the image of the quadrilateral shown above under the action of $T?$
questions.worked_solution:
Recall that for any linear transformation $T$ with associated $2\times 2$ matrix $T,$ we have one of the following three possibilities:

- If $T$ is non-singular, i.e., $det(T)\ne 0,$ then the image of a two-dimensional object is a two-dimensional object. In particular, the image of a polygon with $n$ vertices is a polygon with $n$ vertices.

- If $T$ is singular, i.e., $det(T)=0,$ we have two additional subcases:

- If $T$ has at least one nonzero entry, then the image of a two-dimensional object is a one-dimensional line segment.

- If $T$ is the zero matrix, then the image of a two-dimensional object is the point $(0,0),$ the origin of the coordinate system.

With that in mind, let's examine our transformation.

Computing the determinant of $T,$ we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}det(T) & =|\begin{aligned}-1 & 1 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}| \\  & =-1\cdot 1-0\cdot 1 \\  & =-1.\end{aligned}
$$

So, we have a nonsingular matrix. Therefore, the image of our object under the action of  $T$ is a quadrilateral.

choices.value: The origin $O$ of the coordinate system
A point, different from the origin
